question.problem:
Let $\mathbf{X} = [X_1, X_2,X_3]^T$ be a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find the distribution of $Y = X_1 -2X_2 +4 X_3.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $\mathbf{X} =  [X_1, X_2, \ldots, X_k]^T$ is a multivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma,$ then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y= \mathbf c^T \mathbf X = \sum_{i=1}^k c_i X_i
$$

is a normally distributed random variable, where $\mathbf c$ is any $k\times 1$ column vector, and  

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu , \\ Var[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, since we wish to know the distribution of $Y = X_1 -2X_2 +4 X_3,$ we have 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227571/assets/129ff41cb0fc5917efdc4f990d3d2efeb7546911eadb52340156f1ddc4f9d92f.svg)

Therefore, for the mean of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & ={c}^{T}\mu  \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =1-4+4 \\  & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

and for the variance of $Y,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[Y] & ={c}^{T}Σc \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}12 \\ 3 \\ 14\end{aligned}] \\  & =12-6+56 \\  & =62.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
Y\sim N(1,62).
$$
